A1.1 Module 5 Session 4B — Production & Fluency 75–90 min
🔥 💪 ⚡ 🎯 🏆 5 badges · M5 S4B · Full production — come ready 🎉 All 5 badges — S4B done! M5 exit is next.
§1
Hot Take · Opinion Opener
Deeper questions · Can / Like / Need under real conversational pressure
5–8 min
⚡ Teacher Note — S4B Opening
S4B is the last production session before the M5 exit. Students should feel the increased pressure. Say: "Today is the hardest session in M5. If you can do this, you can do the exit. No notes. No Spanish. Full English from the first second. Let's go."
Hot Take 1: "When someone says 'Can I borrow your charger?' — they're really saying 'I need your charger.' CAN and NEED are the same thing here."
T–S · Agree or disagree · Use CAN or NEED in your answer
Hot Take 2: "Mexican professionals say 'I can do it' too often — and then can't deliver. It's a cultural problem with the word CAN."
S–S · Debate with partner · Include a real example from your job
Hot Take 3: "In a job interview, saying 'I like the team, the projects, and the office location' is more impressive than 'I like working here.'"
Class · Why does specificity matter? · Connect to LIKE + noun (no gerund)
§2
Pitch & Debate Round
Harder scenarios · Integrated can / like / need · No scaffolding
12–15 min
⚡ Teacher Note — Pitch Round S4B
These scenarios are harder than S3B. Students must use can, like, and need together — not separately. Push back on every answer: "Can you give me a specific example?" / "You said you like the team — what exactly do you like about them?" Vague answers don't score points.
🎯 Scenario 1 — The Performance Review (T–S)
Your manager (Teacher) is doing your 6-month performance review at Vertex Logistics. They ask: "Tell me honestly — what can you do well, what can't you do yet, what do you like most about this role, and what do you need from me to grow?"

Student answers all 4 questions in 90 seconds. No notes.
Scoring: 1 pt per can · 1 pt per can't + honest reason · 1 pt per like + specific noun · 1 pt per need + why. Target: 8+ points in 90 seconds.
⚔️ Scenario 2 — The Lunch Order Showdown (S–S)
Partner A and B are ordering for a team of 10 people from the cafeteria at Vertex. Each must order for 5 people — using different phrases, different foods, and saying what each person likes. No person can like the same thing twice.
PARTNER A — Orders 1–5
💡 "Can I get a coffee and a sandwich for Ana? She likes coffee in the morning."
💡 "I'd like a salad for Marco — he likes salad and fruit."
💡 "Does the cafeteria have rice? Pedro needs something hot."
PARTNER B — Orders 6–10
💡 "I'm not really into this menu — can I get something different for Diana?"
💡 "I need two bottles of water and one tea — that's all, thanks."
💡 "Can I get bread and chicken for the last two? They like simple food."
🔗 Scenario 3 — The New Employee Orientation (Class)
Each student is a new employee at Vertex Logistics. The HR manager (Teacher) goes around the room and asks each person ONE question. The catch: the student must answer using ALL THREE structures — can, like, and need — in their answer.
Sample questions: "What can you bring to this team?" · "Do you like this type of work?" · "What do you need from us?" · "Can you work with international clients?" · "What do you like about your previous job?" — Any answer that doesn't include all 3 structures = 0 pts.
§3
Relay Round · Integrated Chains
Harder than S3B · Must use can + like + need in same chain
10 min
🔗 Relay 1 — The Perfect Colleague
Build a description of the perfect colleague at Vertex Logistics. Each student adds ONE sentence. Alternate: CAN sentence → LIKE sentence → NEED sentence → repeat.
Student 1 (CAN): "The perfect colleague can speak English and Spanish."
Student 2 (LIKE): "They like ___________________________________________"
Student 3 (NEED): "They need ___________________________________________"
Student 4 (CAN): "They can ____________________________________________"
Student 5 (LIKE): "They like ___________________________________________"
Student 6 (NEED): "But they don't need ________________________________"
📌 Strict rotation: CAN → LIKE → NEED → repeat. Wrong structure = restart from that student. The "don't need" at the end is the bonus challenge — negative NEED.
🔗 Relay 2 — Monday Morning at the Office
It's Monday 8 AM at Vertex Logistics. Each student says what they can do today, what they like about Mondays (or don't), and what they need. All in one sentence per student.
Starter: "Today I can finish the inventory report. I like Monday mornings — the office is quiet. I need a coffee first."
Student 2: "Today I can _______. I like _______ / I'm not really into _______. I need _______."
Student 3: "Today I can _______. I like _______. I need _______."
Student 4: "Today I can _______. I don't like _______. I need _______."
Student 5: "Today I can _______. I like _______. I don't need _______ — I already have it."
📌 Each student MUST use all three: can, like, need. One sentence each. 5 seconds per student. Student 5 must use the negative (don't need) — the hardest slot. Rotate who gets slot 5.
🔗 Relay 3 — The Cafeteria Survey
Teacher plays the cafeteria manager doing a customer survey. Each student must answer 3 questions — fast. No hesitation. All answers use like + noun (no gerunds).
Teacher asks: "What do you like for lunch?" → Student answers in 5 seconds.
Teacher asks: "Does your colleague like coffee or tea?" → Student answers for a real colleague.
Teacher asks: "What does your manager need from the cafeteria?" → Student answers with need.

Repeat with next student. Different colleague/manager each time. No repeated items.
📌 Error types to track: (1) gerund after like = ❌, (2) missing 3rd person S on likes/needs = ❌, (3) using "want" instead of "need" when teacher asks about need = note but don't penalize at A1.1.
§4
Speed Round · 9 Cards
Harder situations · Integrated structures · 2 pts for explanation
8–10 min
Card 01
Your US manager emails: "Quick — can your team deliver the Monterrey order by Friday?" Answer honestly. You CAN, but you need 2 more people.
✅ CAN + NEED: "Yes, we can deliver by Friday — but we need two more people on the warehouse team. Can you authorize that?" Combines ability + requirement + request. Professional grade.
Card 02
You're at a client lunch. The server asks: "And for you?" You want water, salad, and chicken. Use TWO different request phrases.
✅ TWO PHRASES: "I'd like a water and a salad, please. Can I also get the chicken? That's all, thanks." I'd like + Can I get + That's all = complete professional order.
Card 03
In your LinkedIn profile, you need one sentence about your skills and one about your preferences at work. No gerunds. Go!
✅ LINKEDIN: "I can manage cross-functional teams and use SAP. I like challenge, responsibility, and international work." Two clean sentences. Skills (CAN) + Preferences (LIKE + nouns). Publishable.
Card 04
Your colleague says: "Can you work this Saturday?" You can — but only in the morning. And you need to leave by noon.
✅ CAN + NEED: "Yes, I can work Saturday morning — but I need to leave by noon. Is that okay?" CAN with condition + NEED as requirement + question = honest and professional.
Card 05
Someone offers you fast food at a team lunch. You don't like it. Be polite — use the coloquial phrase AND ask for something else.
✅ COLLOQUIAL + REQUEST: "I'm not really into fast food, thanks — can I get a salad instead? Or maybe fruit?" Polite refusal + alternative request. No "I don't like" needed.
Card 06
Your new intern asks: "What does the operations manager like?" Tell them — but use 3rd person correctly.
✅ 3RD PERSON: "She likes efficiency, data, and direct communication. She doesn't like long meetings without results." LIKES + S for 3rd person. Specific nouns. Zero gerunds.
Card 07
You're applying for a promotion. In 2 sentences: what you can do that your colleague can't, and what you like about leadership.
✅ CAN + LIKE: "I can manage conflict and I can present to senior leadership — skills my colleague is still developing. I like responsibility and I like the challenge of making decisions." Compare + prefer with nouns.
Card 08
Your HR manager asks: "What do you need to be more productive at work?" Give 3 real, specific things.
✅ NEED (x3): "I need a better monitor, I need access to the new system, and I need 30 minutes of quiet time in the morning." Three specific, professional NEED statements. Not vague, not abstract.
Card 09
⚡ FINAL CHALLENGE: You have 30 seconds. Introduce yourself to a client using CAN, LIKE, and NEED — all in one speech. No notes.
✅ INTEGRATED: "Hi — I'm [name], coordinator at Vertex Logistics. I can manage your account and I can communicate in English. I like precision and client relationships. I need your specifications by Thursday to confirm the order. Any questions?"
§5
Solo Challenge · The Exit Rehearsal
4-minute simulation of the M5 exit task · No notes · Full integration
15 min
📋 Solo Challenge — M5 Exit Rehearsal
This is the same format as the M5 exit task. You are at Vertex Logistics, Celaya. Your US regional director has 4 minutes with you before their flight. They want to know who you are, what you do, and if you're ready for the next level.

No slides. No notes. Just you and the language you've built over M5.
1
Open with a professional self-introduction: name, role, company. Use CAN to name your top 3 skills immediately.
2
Tell them what you LIKE about your work — 3 specific things. All nouns. No gerunds. If the director hears "I like working…" — deduct 2 pts.
3
Tell them honestly what you CAN'T do yet — and what you NEED to get there. One limitation + one specific need.
4
Take the director to the cafeteria. Order for both of you using "Can I get…" and "I'd like…". Close with "That's all, thanks."
5
End the conversation professionally: ask the director one question using "Can you…?" or "Do you like…?"
📊 Assessment Rubric — Click each when student completes it
CriterionPtsCheck
Professional intro + 3 specific CAN skills immediately — not generic/ 2Specific = "I can use SAP" / Generic = "I can work hard"
3 LIKE statements using nouns — zero gerunds/ 2Automatic -2 for any "I like working/doing/managing"
Honest CAN'T + specific NEED to fix it/ 1Both must be present — not just one
Cafeteria order with 2 different request phrases + "That's all"/ 1Can I get + I'd like + closing phrase
Closed with a question to the director using CAN or DO YOU LIKE/ 1Initiative = professional bonus
Zero "can + to" errors — base verb always after can/ 1Zero tolerance — this was the S3A target
Spoke 4 full minutes — no pauses over 5 seconds/ 2Fluency criterion — not about grammar
Total: 0 / 10 pts
4 min · No notes · 5 requirements · 10 pts max · Badge b4 on completion
🎧 Model Monologue — Play AFTER the solo · Students identify all structures
After each student attempts the solo, play this once. Class counts: How many CAN? How many LIKE? How many NEED? Who got more than Sofia?
Sofia's Director Meeting — Vertex Logistics, Celaya
A1.1 · M5 · S4B · Voice: Juliet (Customer Care) · Monologue · ≈ 195 words
0:00 / 0:00

SOFIA REYES — VERTEX LOGISTICS — M5 S4B SOLO MODEL

Good morning! I'm Sofia Reyes, Operations Coordinator at Vertex Logistics here in Celaya. Thank you for taking the time to meet with me.

Let me tell you what I can do. I can manage the daily operations for three production lines. I can use Excel and SAP — and I can communicate with our suppliers in English. I can't design the new logistics system yet — I need training in the new software. But I can learn fast.

What do I like about this job? I like the challenge — every day is different. I like the team — we work really well together. And I like the responsibility. I don't like routine work, so this role is perfect for me.

Shall we go to the cafeteria? Can I get a coffee and a chicken sandwich for you, and I'd like a water and a salad for me. That's all, thanks.

Before you leave — can I ask you something? Do you like the new inventory system? I need your feedback to improve our process.

📎 ElevenLabs · Voice: Juliet (Customer Care) · Speed: 0.78 · A1.1 M5 S4B · ≈ 195 words / ≈ 75 sec · Monologue
Sofia uses CAN to describe 3 specific skills — not generic abilities like "work hard."
Sofia says "I like the challenge, the team, and the responsibility" — three nouns, zero gerunds.
Sofia uses both "Can I get…" and "I'd like…" in the cafeteria — and closes with "That's all, thanks."
Sofia ends the conversation without asking a question — she just thanks the director and leaves.

⚡ Teacher Note — S4B Is the Last Production Session
Students who score 28+ pts today are ready for the M5 exit. Below 20 pts: schedule a 15-min review before S5. The exit task (S5) uses the same rubric as the Solo Challenge today — so today's score predicts the exit score. Tell students this. It changes how they perform.
§7
Wrap-Up · Certificate & My Win
M5 S4 done · One session left · Come ready for the exit
5–8 min
01
Integration is the skill. Can alone = basic. Like alone = basic. Need alone = basic. Can + like + need in one conversation = professional English. That's what you did today. That's A1.1 mastery.
02
Nouns protect you. "I like responsibility" is always correct. "I like being responsible" invites A2.1 grammar you don't need yet. At A1.1, nouns after like are your shield. Use them.
03
S5 is the exit. Same scenario, same rubric, real stakes. The students who did best today will lead the S5 exit. Study your weak points this week. One session left.
✅ I Can Now…
I can introduce myself to a director in English using can, like, and need — without notes.
I can describe 3 real, specific skills using CAN — not just "I can work hard."
I can order for multiple people at a cafeteria using different request phrases.
I can use LIKE + noun 3 times without accidentally using a gerund.
I can do the M5 exit task — I practiced the full scenario today and I know what to expect.
